subtopic: Euler Form, De Moivre's Theorem & Roots of a Complex Number
title: Worked: all cube roots of 8i

board_content.text: Find all cube roots of $8i$. First, $8i=8e^{i\pi/2}$.
Three roots, evenly spaced 120 degrees apart on radius 2.

segments_english.text: Let's run the full nth-roots method on a clean example: all cube roots of eight i.
First put eight i in Euler form. Its modulus is eight and its argument is pi over two, so eight i is eight times e to the i pi over two.
The radius of the roots is the cube root of eight, which is two. The angles are pi over two plus two k pi, all divided by three, for k equals zero, one, two.
Stepping k gives three angles: pi over six, five pi over six, and three pi over two.
The first root is two times cosine pi over six plus i sine pi over six, which works out to root three plus i.
The second is two times cosine five pi over six plus i sine five pi over six, which is minus root three plus i.
The third is two times cosine three pi over two plus i sine three pi over two, which is minus two i.
So three roots, each on a circle of radius two, evenly spaced one hundred twenty degrees apart. That even spacing is your built-in check that you found them all.

segments_hinglish.text: Full nth-roots method ek clean example par chalate hain: eight i ke saare cube roots.
Pehle eight i ko Euler form mein daalo. Iska modulus hai eight aur argument hai pi over two, to eight i hai eight times e to the i pi over two.
Roots ka radius hai eight ka cube root, jo hai two. Angles hain pi over two plus two k pi, poora divided by three, k barabar zero, one, two ke liye.
k step karne se teen angles milte hain: pi over six, five pi over six, aur three pi over two.
Pehla root hai two times cosine pi over six plus i sine pi over six, jo banta hai root three plus i.
Doosra hai two times cosine five pi over six plus i sine five pi over six, jo hai minus root three plus i.
Teesra hai two times cosine three pi over two plus i sine three pi over two, jo hai minus two i.
To teen roots, har ek radius two ke circle par, evenly spaced one hundred twenty degrees apart. Wo even spacing aapka built-in check hai ki aapne sab dhoondh liye.
